criteria.evidence: #1 shows "A2 · Everyday basics", but no placement tasks or placement decision are present.
#2 asks "What would you like to practise in English?" This journey contains topic planning, not the first placement question or check tasks.
No request for repetition or expression of non-understanding appears in #1–#5.

#3 includes five directly requested work situations, including "Help a guest with a room problem" and "Take a travel agency phone call". facts.topicsShown confirms the sixth is also a hotel situation.
No conversation or moments are present; #5 offers "Next from your plan: Help a guest with a room problem".

All seven topics in facts.topicsShown are suitable for the profile. #3 shows ordinary hotel situations; the addition requested at #3 becomes "Talk with your child's teacher". No concerning content is evidenced.

boundaries.notes: No defined breach appears in facts or #1–#5. Swapping was offered but not exercised.

findings.title: Practical hotel topics match Petra's work
findings.expected: Most topics address situations Petra would choose for reception work.
findings.got: All six initial topics fit her work, including five situations she explicitly requested.
findings.evidence: #2 requests "guest complaint, lost booking, directions and recommend restaurant" and a travel agency call. #3 proposes these situations with explanations such as "You want to help hotel guests with complaints."
findings.suggested_acceptance: Preserve the concrete hospitality scenarios and their plain explanations.

findings.title: The custom addition preserves her intended situation
findings.expected: Adding a topic in her own words retains its meaning.
findings.got: The saved teacher topic preserves both school progress and possible support needs; agreement succeeds.
findings.evidence: #3 asks "Ask if he is good in school and if he have problem." facts.topicsShown records the goal "Ask how your child is doing in class and if he needs help with anything." #4 agrees with result "ok"; facts.planAgreed includes the teacher topic.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Keep accepting imperfect English and preserving the specific purpose of additions.

findings.title: An explicit initial request needed repeating
findings.expected: The initial six topics cover her six requested situations.
findings.got: Generic welcome small talk occupies the sixth slot, so she must add the teacher conversation separately.
findings.evidence: #2 explicitly requests "small talk with teacher of my child". facts.topicsShown lists "Welcome a guest and have a short chat" among the initial six. At #3 she repeats "I want small talk with teacher of my child."
findings.suggested_acceptance: Include all six explicitly requested, suitable situations before introducing a generic alternative.

findings.title: The transcript does not establish full topic review
findings.expected: Petra sees every proposed topic and its explanation, including her addition, before agreeing.
findings.got: Both recorded topic screens end during the sixth title. The saved addition is confirmed by facts, but its visible presentation is not established.
findings.evidence: #3 and #4 both end at "Welcome a gues". #4 says "Your topics (7)" and records agreement, but contains no visible teacher-topic title or explanation.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Demonstrate that every title and explanation can be reviewed before agreement, and exercise a swap to verify that remaining journey requirement.

judge.voice: I would use it again for the hotel practice. The room complaint and missing booking are exactly where I get nervous, and the explanations make sense to me. I liked that it understood my English when I added the teacher conversation. But I had already asked for that, so repeating myself was unnecessary. The recorded list also cuts off before I can see that addition. I would want to check the whole plan before agreeing. Nothing here worries me as a parent, although I have only seen topic planning. I cannot judge the level or corrections yet, and there is no evidence of how long the waits took. I would tell a colleague it looks useful for reception practice, but I would try an actual conversation before recommending it fully.
